title: [Collection of musical treatises]
shelf_note: A 15th-century music-theory manuscript (chant notation, mensural/plainchant treatise). No tradition or collection is assigned; it is outside the core esoteric shelves, though defensible as early modern science. The fit cannot be judged properly because the scan unit is wrong (see structure).
structure_note: Each 'page' is a microfilm strip of about six openings (12 leaves) at 2000x220 px. The whole manuscript is 9 such strips, so one record = ~12 leaves, and at this resolution no word is legible. This is a page-unit and catalogue-format defect (I5/I7 shape): the text on each record cannot be a reading of its image. pages 9 / OCR 9 / translated 8.

ocr_errors.image: Strip of six openings, script illegible at 220 px height; the notation visible is single-line chant/neumes on staves with text, not four-part Tenor/Bassus/Cantus/Altus polyphony
ocr_errors.problem: Polyphonic voice-part texts invented (and duplicated per voice); not readable from this image

tr_errors.problem: A faithful translation of text that is not on the page; a reader is told this strip says things it does not

ocr_errors.problem: The same invented paragraph repeated verbatim for four different openings

ocr_errors.problem: A generic treatise on instruments made up from expectation; not readable from the image

book_verdict: Not readable as published. Each record is a microfilm strip of about 12 leaves at a resolution where no word is legible, and the OCR fills each one with plausible generic music theory, including one paragraph repeated four times. Hold the text and re-source the images leaf by leaf.

title: Epithalamium in nuptiis gabrielis salamancae atque Elisabetae eberstaniae
shelf_note: Neo-Latin wedding poem (Riccardo Sbruglio for Gabriel Salamanca, 1520s). A genuine early-modern Latin source, but it has no tradition or collection and nothing esoteric about it.
structure_note: 8 pages, all OCR'd and translated. 'published: Unknown' could be filled in (c. 1520s). OCR self-tags the printed italic as 'handwritten'.

ocr_errors.image: Printed italic type, signature A ij

tr_errors.source: Quam pariunt uestri candida nympha lares
tr_errors.english: Which you, bright nymph, bring forth to your homes
tr_errors.problem: Subject reversed: 'which your household gods bring forth, a bright nymph' (i.e. her house produced her)

tr_errors.source: Nec uestras Athesis fortunas dignaque nescit / Nominat er geminis
tr_errors.english: Nor does the Adige remain unaware of your fortunes and dignity, / And it names you, ennobled in two ways
tr_errors.problem: Loose; the couplet is about names ennobled 'ter geminis modis', and the translation smooths it

ocr_errors.ocr: Pan animos tum addes tum adimes.
ocr_errors.image: Pan animos tum addēs tū adimēs.
ocr_errors.problem: Abbreviation marks dropped silently; reading fine

tr_errors.source: Et conuiua datis defit ubique cibis.
tr_errors.english: And the guest is never lacking in provided foods.
tr_errors.problem: Reversed: the guest 'gives out' (is overcome) before the food served; the point is excess, not sufficiency

tr_errors.source: admittunt ignea Fauni, / Spicula Pan blandum datque capitque melos.
tr_errors.english: the Fauns admit the fiery ones, / Pan gives bland darts and takes back the melody
tr_errors.problem: Line division misparsed: the Fauns take in fiery darts; Pan gives and takes up a sweet song

tr_errors.source: Horrida discutiunt apices tormenta niuales
tr_errors.english: The bristling storms scatter the snowy peaks
tr_errors.problem: 'tormenta' = artillery (the mock battle at the wedding), not storms

tr_errors.source: Quartum uirtutis precium Dipolde reportas, / Halle
tr_errors.english: Dipoldus, you report the fourth prize ... / Halle, with trumpets
tr_errors.problem: 'reportas' = carry off; 'Halle' is the vocative of Hallus (the marginal name), rendered as if a separate word

tr_errors.source: Cui praefert Mauors Mercuriusque facem.
tr_errors.english: To which Mars and Mercury prefer the torch.
tr_errors.problem: 'praefert facem' = carry the torch before (lead the dance), not 'prefer'

tr_errors.source: Pugnaces inter tam sanguine clarus Iberos, / Quam meritis rectam quaeris ad astra uiam.
tr_errors.english: Famous for such blood among the pugnacious Iberians, / As you seek the straight path to the stars by your merits.
tr_errors.problem: The tam...quam construction (as famous by blood as by merit) is garbled

tr_errors.source: Quae nunc Augustas edit et auget opes
tr_errors.english: Which now edits and increases the Augustan riches
tr_errors.problem: 'edit' = brings forth, not 'edits'

book_verdict: The transcription is excellent, close to letter-perfect against clear printed italic. The translation is readable, but several couplets of the elegiacs are misparsed (a reversed sense, artillery read as 'storms'). Showable with a draft-translation caveat.

title: Argumenta in librum Psalmorum, Estheræ Inglis manu exarata Londini 1606
shelf_note: Esther Inglis's calligraphic manuscript of Latin verse arguments to the Psalms, with painted flowers. A fine primary source, but devotional/calligraphic rather than part of any esoteric tradition, and no collection is assigned.
structure_note: 214 pages, 214 OCR'd, 108 translated. That is probably the text leaves (versos and blanks may be skipped), but half the book untranslated is worth checking. The pages sampled are single leaves photographed with a colour bar, and include mirror-written pages, which the OCR handles.

tr_errors.source: Splendida describit sua sint quae insignia David
tr_errors.english: David describes what his distinctions are
tr_errors.problem: 'splendida' (splendid) dropped

tr_errors.source: Ille suis etenim munera laeta dabit.
tr_errors.english: For he will surely give joyful gifts to his own.
tr_errors.problem: Fine

ocr_errors.problem: Psalm number wrong (58 for 68); the page's one identifier misnames which psalm the argument belongs to, and the translation's keywords repeat 'Psalm 58'

ocr_errors.ocr: Adnotet hic etenim propriam defendere gentem
ocr_errors.image: Assolet hic etenim propriam defendere gentem

tr_errors.source: Adnotet hic etenim propriam defendere gentem
tr_errors.english: Let him note here that he defends his own people
tr_errors.problem: Follows the misread; the source says God is wont to defend his own people

other.note: OCR stores a <meta> 'The text is written from right to left in mirror image' and the translation <summary>/<keywords> tags

tr_errors.source: Laudibus et meritis discant celebrare Tonantem
tr_errors.english: Let them learn to celebrate the Thunderer ... with praises and merits
tr_errors.problem: Should be 'with deserved praises' (laudibus ut meritis); follows the misread

book_verdict: Clear, short verse texts, mostly read well, including the mirror-written leaves. But page 111 gives the wrong psalm number (LVIII for LXVIII) and a misread verb that skews the translation. Showable after correcting that leaf.

title: [Blockbook] Calendarium magistri Johannis de Gamundia de 1439
shelf_note: Johannes of Gmunden's woodcut calendar with zodiac signs and labours of the months: early astronomy and astrology, a reasonable fit for early modern science and the BPH holdings.
structure_note: The catalogue says 'published: 1439' but 'place_published: z.p|[18e eeuw]', which implies an 18th-century impression or copy of the blocks. Dating the object 1439 overstates it (I7). 18 pages, 8 translated.

ocr_errors.ocr: | | d | Hic incipit iohannes | | / | | e | De Gamundia | |
ocr_errors.image: 'Hec Magister Johannes / De Gamundia' spanning the foot of the February column
ocr_errors.problem: The maker's line is misread as 'Here begins John'; the translation says 'Here begins John Of Gmunden'
Saints shifted or misread against their days: Gregory is put on 9 March instead of 12 March
Wrong saint; the translation then invents 'Sixtus, Martyr and King'

ocr_errors.ocr: Golden-number column, January rows 4-5: 'v' on row 4, blank on row 5
ocr_errors.problem: Golden numbers shifted by a row in places, which breaks the computus column

ocr_errors.image: Hour numbers in the roundel corners (8/16, 10/14, 12/12) and the January zodiac roundel (Aquarius)
ocr_errors.problem: Day/night hour figures and one zodiac roundel omitted

tr_errors.source: Hic incipit iohannes / De Gamundia
tr_errors.english: Here begins John / Of Gmunden
tr_errors.problem: Faithful to the misread; it reads as an incipit, where the source names Master John as the calendar's author

ocr_errors.problem: Wrong saints on 2 July's octave row

ocr_errors.ocr: Right-hand letter column (e.g. 'f g y A z 3 c d' in August)

tr_errors.source: Oswaldi. Dña
tr_errors.english: Oswald [and] Afra
tr_errors.problem: Invented saint for an abbreviation (Afra is on 7 August, two rows below)

tr_errors.source: Sēte rōe
tr_errors.english: Saint Zoe <note>original: "Sēte rōe"</note>
tr_errors.problem: Correct guess with a visible note; fine

ocr_errors.image: a saint's name ('Iuliani ...'), vigil not written

ocr_errors.ocr: Right-hand letter column in December 'q r s t u...'

tr_errors.source: Stationis mār
tr_errors.english: Stationis Martyr <note>Likely refers to a feast associated with a station church or St. Anastasia.</note>
tr_errors.problem: Speculative gloss on a misread name

tr_errors.source: Incolōr
tr_errors.english: Incolarum <note>This name likely refers to a local or specific minor feast.</note>
tr_errors.problem: Speculative gloss on a misread

book_verdict: The layout and the woodcut descriptions are right, and most saints are right. But each month has several saints misread or put on the wrong day, and the golden-number and letter columns are unreliable, which matters in a calendar. The 1439 date also overstates what looks catalogued as an 18th-century impression.

title: Liber Piccatriciae
shelf_note: An 18th-century manuscript copy of the Latin Picatrix: core astrological magic.
structure_note: Printed page numbers sit a constant 10 below the record numbers (117->107, 233->223, 347->337), which is consistent. 467 pages, 464 OCR'd, 451 translated. Nothing stands out.

ocr_errors.ocr: <margin> naturalis / quemadmodum / finibus, qui / annulis, ... dam </margin>
ocr_errors.image: Line-ends of the facing left page visible in the gutter
ocr_errors.problem: The neighbour page's strip is read as a marginal note on this page (the translation drops it)

tr_errors.source: propter convenientiam
tr_errors.english: on account of the convenience
tr_errors.problem: 'convenientia' = agreement/affinity

ocr_errors.image: 'breviter compleatur,' with folio number 223 in the top corner
ocr_errors.problem: Page number merged into the text

tr_errors.source: in tantum quod 224 praecesserunt antiquorum sapientum Indi de verbo ad verbum
tr_errors.english: writing so much that the 224 [pages/chapters] which preceded [were based on] the ancient sages of India, word for word
tr_errors.problem: The famous Picatrix claim is that the compiler drew on 224 books of the ancient sages. The bracketed '[pages/chapters]' and '[were based on]' invent a different sense

ocr_errors.ocr: Recipe sudorem tuum et pilum bene mundum
ocr_errors.image: ℞ sudorem tuum et pelvim bene mundam
ocr_errors.problem: 'pelvim' (basin) read as 'pilum' (hair); the translation says 'a clean hair'

ocr_errors.ocr: ibidem ponas seraphis quos sunt sub suis pedibus
ocr_errors.image: ibidem ponas de rasuris quae sunt sub suis pedibus

ocr_errors.ocr: quando D est cum O ... cum Q ... quando D est O O
ocr_errors.image: astronomical symbols: Moon with Sun, Moon with Venus, Moon in conjunction with Sun

tr_errors.source: seraphis
tr_errors.english: the <term>seraphis</term> <gloss>possibly meaning burning ones or a specific plant</gloss>
tr_errors.problem: Speculative gloss stacked on a misread

tr_errors.source: quando D est cum Q ... quando D est O O
tr_errors.english: when the moon is with the dragon's tail ... given when the moon is the moon
tr_errors.problem: Venus rendered as 'the dragon's tail'; 'when the moon is the moon' is nonsense covering the conjunction symbol

tr_errors.source: Recipe ... pilum bene mundum
tr_errors.english: Take your sweat and a clean hair
tr_errors.problem: Follows the misread (basin)

book_verdict: A good transcription of a clear 18th-century hand, and a readable translation of the core Picatrix. The weak spots are the astrological symbols (flattened, then mistranslated), a few misread nouns in the recipes, and one invented gloss on the '224 books' passage. Showable as a draft.
